messages:
maria: FYI I'm seeing steady resident memory growth on prod during long streaming sessions that use tool loops. Not a sharp leak, more like slow -> 500MB over ~2 hours for a single session.

alex: Can you paste the reproducer and a quick pprof snapshot?

maria: Repro is a simulated chat that triggers tool calls every ~30s (query->tool->response->append) - attach logs and a heap profile from pprof that I grabbed at +0m, +30m, +90m.

maria: logs: 
```
[2026-03-10T09:12:03Z] session=ses_83 appendTokens count=120 kv_residency=312 kv_pages=8
[2026-03-10T09:42:03Z] session=ses_83 appendTokens count=380 kv_residency=728 kv_pages=12
[2026-03-10T10:42:03Z] session=ses_83 appendTokens count=1120 kv_residency=1640 kv_pages=18
```

maria: pprof snapshot (+90m):
```
heap profile: 96.4MB heap in 1423 allocs
     24.0MB  24.9%  24.9%  github.com/redwood/kv.(*Shard).AllocEntry
     18.4MB  19.1%  44.0%  runtime.mallocgc
     12.0MB  12.4%  56.4%  github.com/redwood/streaming.(*Session).appendChunk
      8.0MB   8.3%  64.7%  github.com/redwood/kv.(*Cache).evictCandidate
```

maria: Note kv_residency increases monotonically even when kv_pages doesn't spike. Looks like fragmentation or small-object churn in Shard allocator.

kevin: That pattern smells like partial eviction where we free entries but underlying pages stay allocated (hugepages-like behavior). Are we using jemalloc/jemalloc background purge?

maria: We're on system malloc (glibc) in hosted for this bucket. I ran `pmap` during test:
```
000055c3b6f00000   104K r--p 00000000 00:00 0                          [anon]
000055c3b7000000  24.0M rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [heap]
00007f2a1d000000   16M rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [kv-pages]
```

ben: Could be that our KV entries are variable sized and we're reallocating lots of small buffers causing internal fragmentation. Do we reuse buffers when we evict?

maria: Current path: insert -> store copy -> on-evict free. No freelist for variable-size buffers.

alex: Two quick experiments to try: 1) enable jemalloc with background thread purge and run same workload, 2) change shard allocator to keep a small per-shard freelist for up to N buffers to test reuse. Either should reduce resident growth if fragmentation/reuse is the cause.

maria: I did 1) locally with jemalloc (MALLOC_CONF="background_thread:true,lg_dirty_mult:16") and reran. Resident growth flattened to ~80MB max vs 500MB before. Heap profile shifted: AllocEntry dropped to 6MB.

infra-bot: CI run started: infra/kv/residency-repro #342 (jenkins)

kevin: Great signal. That suggests fragmentation/paging rather than a true code-path leak. But we should still test memory reclamation semantics on our target distro (glibc + old kernel) since hosted runs that.

maria: Filed INF-1879 with reproducer and heaps: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1879

alex: For short-term mitigation we can: - flip jemalloc on Dedicated host images - add per-shard freelist mempool as opt-in flag - expose `kv.reserve` config to pre-warm larger contiguous pages. Longer-term: consider arena-level compaction or switch to slab-like fixed-size buckets for common sizes.

ben: I can prototype a freelist patch: keep last 64 buffers per shard up to 4KB and reuse on insert. That should be low-risk perf-wise.

maria: Repro results with freelist prototype look promising: resident capped and steady over 3h. I'll drop benchmark numbers in the ticket.

ci-bot: Build #342 passed unit+integration; perf bench still running.

alex: Nice work. Next steps: 1) get infra to trial jemalloc on one Dedicated pool, 2) land freelist behind runtime flag and A/B on production traffic with the canary rollout. Also add telemetry: kv_residency, kv_frag_pct, freelist_hits.

maria: I'll add telemetry and a small eval to quantify token throughput/latency impact. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kevin: One more note: avoid large-scoped gc pauses - prefer background eviction/compaction. We'll coordinate with eng-sre for rollout windows.

maria: Updated ticket with pprof svgs and a short reproducer script: `tools/repro/kv_residency_repro.sh`.

ben: PR incoming for freelist prototype later today.

maria: Closing loop here — I'll post final perf numbers and patch link once CI finishes.
